evidence.snippet: Neurologic signs and symptoms of TBE vary but can include meningeal signs, altered mental status, cognitive dysfunction (e.g., decreased concentration and memory impairment), ataxia, rigidity, tremors, and cranial nerve and limb paresis or palsies.

nodes.description: Following inoculation of TBEV via tick bite into the skin (or across the gastrointestinal tract after dairy ingestion), the virus replicates locally in cutaneous dendritic cells, drains to regional lymph nodes, and establishes a primary viremia that causes the first febrile phase of biphasic illness with transient bone marrow suppression (leukopenia and thrombocytopenia) and mild hepatic injury.

nodes.description: Three-dose primary immunization series with formaldehyde-inactivated, whole-virus European subtype TBE vaccine (TICOVAC / FSME-IMMUN) induces neutralizing antibodies in 99% of seronegative adults (GMT 259 at 21-28 days post-dose 3) and confers 91% to 99% vaccine effectiveness against clinical TBE and hospitalization. Older adults achieve lower post-vaccination neutralizing antibody titers and experience more rapid seroreversion over time.
